title: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act No. 35 of 2019)
name: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act No. 35 of 2019)
organisation: Ministry of Law and Justice & Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
authority: Ministry of Law and Justice & Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
topic: Principal Statutory Framework for Consumer Rights & Consumer Commissions
summary: Enacted by the Parliament of India on 9th August 2019, replacing the 1986 Act. Codifies six statutory consumer rights under Section 2(9), establishes the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), provides product liability (Chapter VI), and establishes the three-tier Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions (District, State, and National).
verified_claims_or_topics: Section 2(9) statutory definitions of six consumer rights
Section 2(7) definition of consumer including e-commerce and direct selling
Section 34, 47, 58 establishing District, State, and National Consumer Commissions
Section 34(2)(d) allowing complaints to be filed where the consumer resides or works
Section 69 two-year limitation period from date of cause of action
Chapter VI Sections 82-87 governing product liability actions
In-person appearance without advocate permitted under the Act
legal_reference: Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 1, Act No. 35 of 2019
notes: Verified against official India Code legislative repository. Primary legal authority for all statutory consumer rights in India.

title: National Consumer Helpline (NCH / INGRAM)
name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH / INGRAM)
organisation: Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, Government of India
authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, Government of India
summary: Central grievance platform operated by the Department of Consumer Affairs for pre-litigation alternate dispute resolution. Facilitates fast convergence with over 800 partner companies to resolve consumer disputes informally without requiring court litigation.
verified_claims_or_topics: Toll-free national helpline shortcode 1915 (and legacy 1800-11-4000)
Operational hours: 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on all days (except national holidays)
WhatsApp grievance registration via +91 8800001915 and SMS to 8800001915
Pre-litigation company convergence mechanism across 800+ registered brands
Distinction: NCH facilitates informal mediation but does not issue binding court orders or award damages
legal_reference: Department of Consumer Affairs Project for Convergence and Alternate Redressal
notes: Verified against consumerhelpline.gov.in and DoCA portal. Recommended first step before filing legal proceedings.

title: e-Jagriti Unified Consumer Redressal & Case Management Portal
name: e-Jagriti Unified Consumer Redressal & Case Management Portal
organisation: Department of Consumer Affairs & National Informatics Centre (NIC)
authority: Department of Consumer Affairs & National Informatics Centre (NIC)
topic: Unified Electronic Consumer Court Filing, Fee Payment & Virtual Hearings
summary: Unified digital case management platform developed by NIC under the Department of Consumer Affairs, integrating e-Daakhil, OCMS, NCDRC CMS, and CONFONET into a single window. Enables consumers to file cases online before District, State, and National Consumer Commissions, upload evidence, pay statutory fees, track case orders, and attend virtual hearings.
verified_claims_or_topics: Unified electronic complaint filing across District (DCDRC), State (SCDRC), and National (NCDRC) Commissions
Online fee payment gateway integration and digital document uploads
Virtual hearing participation via integrated video-conferencing
Real-time case tracking, cause lists, daily orders, and certified judgements access
Integration of e-Daakhil system into unified e-Jagriti architecture
legal_reference: Central initiative of Department of Consumer Affairs and National Informatics Centre
notes: Verified against DoCA official launch release. Represents the modern official portal for consumer judicial filings.

title: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) & BIS Care Portal
name: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) & BIS Care Portal
organisation: Bureau of Indian Standards, Government of India
authority: Bureau of Indian Standards, Government of India
topic: Product Standards, Mandatory ISI Certification & Gold Hallmarking (HUID)
summary: The National Standards Body of India established under the BIS Act, 2016. Formulates Indian Standards, oversees the ISI product certification scheme, Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) for electronic goods, mandatory Hallmarking of gold and silver with 6-digit Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID), and the BIS Care mobile verification application.
verified_claims_or_topics: BIS Care mobile app for verifying ISI license authenticity and electronics CRS R-numbers
6-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) for verifying gold jewellery purity
Mandatory ISI certification for safety-critical consumer products (electronics, helmets, gas appliances)
Online complaint filing against sub-standard products, false hallmarking, and counterfeit standard marks
Consumer right to demand certified products under Right to Safety
legal_reference: Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 (Act No. 11 of 2016)
notes: Verified against bis.gov.in and Manakonline portal.

title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
name: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
organisation: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
topic: E-Commerce Marketplaces, Transparency & Mandatory Grievance Officers
summary: Binding statutory regulations notified under Section 101 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Governs all e-commerce entities selling goods or services to consumers in India, mandating Grievance Officers, 48-hour acknowledgment, 1-month resolution, and fair return/cancellation practices.
verified_claims_or_topics: Rule 4(5) mandatory appointment of Grievance Redressal Officer with published contact info
Rule 4(5) mandatory acknowledgment of any consumer complaint within 48 hours
Rule 4(5) mandatory resolution of consumer grievance within 1 month from date of receipt
Rule 4(8) prohibition on imposing cancellation charges unless entity bears similar charges if they cancel
Mandatory disclosure of seller identity, country of origin, and return/refund terms on marketplace listings
legal_reference: Notification G.S.R. 462(E) dated 23rd July 2020 published in Gazette of India
notes: Verified against official gazette notification on consumeraffairs.gov.in.

title: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023
name: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023
organisation: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), Government of India
authority: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), Government of India
topic: Prohibition of Deceptive UI/UX Design & Digital Consumer Exploitation
summary: Issued by CCPA under Section 18 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 on 30th November 2023. Explicitly defines and prohibits 13 specific dark patterns in user interfaces that subvert consumer autonomy, decision-making, or choice.
verified_claims_or_topics: Explicit prohibition of 13 dark patterns: False Urgency, Basket Sneaking, Confirm Shaming, Forced Action, Subscription Trap, Interface Interference, Bait and Switch, Drip Pricing, Disguised Advertisement, Nagging, Trick Question, SaaS Billing, Rogue Malwares
Applies to all platforms, advertisers, and sellers offering goods/services systematically in India
Classification of deceptive digital design as unfair trade practice under CPA 2019
notes: Verified against CCPA official notification on consumeraffairs.gov.in.

title: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
name: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
organisation: Department of Consumer Affairs, Legal Metrology Division, Government of India
authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, Legal Metrology Division, Government of India
topic: Maximum Retail Price (MRP) Compliance, Ban on Cooling Charges & Net Quantity
summary: Framed under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009. Governs packaging, labeling, and retail pricing of packaged goods. Rule 18(2) strictly bars selling any pre-packaged commodity at a price exceeding the printed MRP. Also prohibits dual MRP labeling for identical goods.
verified_claims_or_topics: Rule 18(2) absolute prohibition on selling pre-packaged commodities above printed MRP
Strict ban on adding chilling or refrigeration fees on top of printed MRP for cold beverages
Prohibition against dual/differential MRP labels on identical pre-packaged goods
Mandatory package declarations: MRP (all taxes inclusive), net weight, expiry/use-by date, manufacturer contact
Judicial exception: Composite dining service at sit-down hotels and restaurants under Supreme Court precedent
legal_reference: Notification G.S.R. 202(E) dated 7th March 2011 as amended
notes: Verified against Legal Metrology Rules on consumeraffairs.gov.in.

title: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of Commissions) Rules, 2021
name: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of Commissions) Rules, 2021
organisation: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India
topic: Pecuniary Jurisdiction Thresholds for Consumer Commissions
summary: Notified under Section 102 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 on 30th December 2021. Established revised pecuniary limits for consumer commissions based strictly on the value of goods or services paid as consideration.
verified_claims_or_topics: District Commission: Entertains complaints where consideration paid does not exceed ₹50 Lakh
State Commission: Entertains complaints where consideration paid exceeds ₹50 Lakh up to ₹2 Crore
National Commission (NCDRC): Entertains complaints where consideration paid exceeds ₹2 Crore
Statutory determination: Pecuniary jurisdiction is based on consideration actually paid, not speculative compensation claimed
notes: Verified against official gazette notification on consumeraffairs.gov.in and PIB release.

Fee of ₹200 for claims above ₹5 Lakh up to ₹10 Lakh
Fee of ₹400 for claims above ₹10 Lakh up to ₹20 Lakh

Right of consumer to draft, file, and argue case in-person without advocate

title: Harmonisation of Turn Around Time (TAT) and Customer Compensation for Failed Transactions

summary: Circular DPSS.CO.PD No.629/02.01.014/2019-20 issued by RBI on September 20, 2019. Harmonises Turn Around Time (TAT) across electronic payment systems and mandates automatic financial compensation directly to customer accounts for resolution delays.

Mandatory auto-compensation of ₹100 per day of delay payable automatically (suo motu) without requiring separate customer claim
Failed ATM cash dispense auto-reversal within T+5 days
Applies across UPI, IMPS, ATM, POS, and digital wallet systems
Right to escalate to RBI Integrated Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in / 14448) after 30 days of unaddressed bank grievance
